# A filter on a dotted path never matches raw items or undeclared paths

## Context

Found while reviewing neomjs/neo#20276, the sorting fix for #20275. The probe ran the engine's own unit setup against `dev` (`3ed29de673`) and against #20276's head (`59e702372f`). Both give the same rows. The filter is `{operator: '>=', property, value: 30}` over two items scoring 20 (id 1) and 50 (id 2), so every row should keep `[2]`:

```
property                         owner                      kept   expected
tp (flat; the probe's control)   Collection, Store R/T      [2]    [2]
stats.score (path into Object)   Collection                 []     [2]
stats.score (path into Object)   Store, Records             []     [2]
stats.score (path into Object)   Store, Turbo               []     [2]
user.score (declared nested)     Store, Records             [2]    [2]
user.score (declared nested)     Store, Turbo               []     [2]
```

R = `autoInitRecords: true`, T = `autoInitRecords: false` (Turbo Mode).

## The Problem

A filter whose `property` is a dotted path keeps nothing unless the item itself exposes that dotted key. Only a Record with a declared nested field does. Turbo Mode stores, plain items in a `Collection`, and paths into `Object` fields filter out every item. The grid header's inline filter takes the column's `dataField` as its property. A dotted column in a Turbo Mode grid therefore filters out every row. After #20276, sorting resolves these paths, but filtering still reads the key directly.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.collection.Filter#decide` reads `recordValue = item[property]` (`src/collection/Filter.mjs`). Every operator uses that one direct read, `typedIncluded` and its `typedKeys` set included.
- `Neo.data.Record#get(field)` resolves an undeclared dotted path through `Neo.ns(field, false, this[dataSymbol])` (`src/data/RecordFactory.mjs`). A declared nested field exposes its dotted getter (`record['address.city']`, `learn/guides/datahandling/Records.md`).
- `grid/header/Button.mjs` builds its inline filter as `store.getFilter(me.dataField, 'header-inline')`.
- #20276 adds `Neo.collection.Sorter.getValue(item, property)`. It reads the key directly first, then, for a dotted string path whose value is `undefined`, tries `item.get(path)` and then `Neo.ns(path, false, item)`. The same PR makes `Store#resolveField` hydrate the declared root of an undeclared dotted path in Turbo Mode without stamping the dotted key.
- Design authority: `learn/guides/datahandling/Grids.md` configures columns with dotted `dataField`s (`{text: 'Firstname', dataField: 'user.firstname'}`). The header filter takes that `dataField` as its property, and #20275 treats a dotted `property` that sorts as a no-op as a bug.

## The Fix

`Filter#decide` reads `recordValue` through the resolver sorting uses after #20276: `Neo.collection.Sorter.getValue(item, property)`, or a neutral static that both classes import if review prefers that. Flat properties keep their one-read fast path. The dotted fallback runs only when the direct read is `undefined`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A filter on a dotted path matches plain items in a `Collection` and raw items in a Turbo Mode `Store` and `TreeStore`: the table's empty rows keep `[2]`. Flat-property filters are unchanged.
- [ ] AC-2: A declared nested field filters the same in Record and Turbo Mode (`user.score` keeps `[2]` in both).
- [ ] AC-3: Unit specs cover AC-1 and AC-2, each red on `dev` before the fix: `test/playwright/unit/collection/` for `Filter`, `test/playwright/unit/data/` for `Store` and `TreeStore`. The existing suites pass.

## Out of Scope

- Sorting by dotted paths: #20275, PR #20276.
- Remote filtering, which the server applies.

## Related

#20275 (sorting, same resolution rule) · PR #20276 (the resolver this builds on) · `examples/grid/nestedRecordFields`.
